breakfast.name: Syrniki (Russian Cottage Cheese Pancakes)
breakfast.description: Russian and Ukrainian cottage cheese pancakes with crispy exterior and fluffy interior, quick and easy to prepare. Can be served sweet with sour cream and honey or savory
ingredients: Sour cream and honey for serving
instructions: Mash cottage cheese in large bowl with fork until smooth
Add eggs, sugar, salt, flour, and baking powder
Drop approximately 1/4 cup batter portions onto flour
Using two forks, roll each portion to coat in flour, then shape into oval patties
Heat 2 tbsp oil in large non-stick skillet over medium heat
Carefully place syrniki in hot oil
Fry 2-3 minutes until golden brown and crispy on bottom
Flip and fry another 2 minutes until golden on second side
Remove to paper towels to drain
Serve hot with dollop of sour cream and drizzle of honey or maple syrup
breakfast.notes: High protein content from cottage cheese makes them very filling. Can be made in under 30 minutes
breakfast.fun_fact: Syrniki are tasty Russian and Ukrainian breakfast or dessert with crispy exterior and fluffy interior. They have been part of Russian cuisine for centuries
alternatives: Serve with jam instead of honey

common_swaps.egg: flax egg (1 tbsp ground flax + 3 tbsp water)

stepHelp: Small curd or well-mashed cottage cheese gives the smoothest texture — press out any excess liquid first if your cheese looks watery.
The batter will be soft and a little sticky — that's normal, the flour coating is what makes it easy to shape.
The flour coating firms up the sticky batter enough to shape by hand — pat gently into a flat oval about 1/2 inch thick.
Resist moving them around — let the bottom fully set and brown before you try to flip, or they can break apart.

variations.title: Berry-Studded
variations.text: Fold fresh or frozen berries into the batter for bursts of fruit in every bite.

variations.title: Raisin Syrniki
variations.text: Add a handful of raisins to the batter for the traditional sweet, chewy addition.

variations.title: Savory Syrniki
variations.text: Skip the sugar, add chopped herbs and a pinch more salt, and serve with sour cream and smoked salmon.

variations.title: Baked Version
variations.text: Bake on a parchment-lined sheet at 375°F for a lower-fat version, flipping once halfway through.

variations.title: Mini Syrniki
variations.text: Make smaller, silver-dollar-sized patties for a fun brunch platter with different toppings.

serveWith.intro: Syrniki are filling enough to be the whole meal, but a few classic toppings and a drink round things out.

items.title: Sour Cream
items.text: The traditional topping — its tang balances the sweetness of the pancakes.

items.title: Honey
items.text: Drizzled on top, it's the classic sweet finish.

items.title: Fresh Berries
items.text: Their brightness cuts through the richness of the cheese.

items.title: Jam
items.text: Any fruit preserve works well spooned over a stack.

items.title: Black Tea
items.text: A strong, unsweetened tea is a traditional pairing that balances the dish's sweetness.

expertTips.title: Drain Watery Cheese
expertTips.text: If your cottage cheese looks wet, drain it in a fine sieve for 15 minutes first — excess moisture makes the batter too sticky to shape.

expertTips.title: Don't Skip the Flour Coating
expertTips.text: It's what lets you shape a soft, sticky batter into neat patties without it sticking to your hands.

expertTips.title: Medium Heat, Patience
expertTips.text: Too hot and the outside burns before the inside cooks through; medium heat gives you a fully golden, crisp exterior with a cooked center.

expertTips.title: High-Protein and Filling
expertTips.text: Cottage cheese makes these unusually filling for pancakes — a smaller portion than you'd expect often does the trick.

storage.title: Fridge
storage.text: Cooked syrniki keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.

storage.title: Freezer
storage.text: Freeze cooked and cooled syrniki in a single layer, then bag for up to 2 months.

storage.title: Reheating
storage.text: Reheat in a skillet over low heat to re-crisp the exterior, or in the oven at 325°F — a microwave will leave them soft.

breakfast.makeAhead: Mix the batter and shape the patties up to a day ahead, keeping them covered in the fridge (dust with a little extra flour first so they don't stick together). Fry them fresh when you're ready to eat for the best texture.

faqs.q: Why did my syrniki fall apart while frying?
faqs.a: The cheese was likely too wet, or they weren't given enough time to set on the first side before flipping. Drain watery cheese first, and let the bottom fully brown before turning.

faqs.q: Can I use ricotta instead of cottage cheese?
faqs.a: Yes, though ricotta is wetter — drain it well first, or you may need a bit more flour to get a shapeable batter.
Traditionally sweet, served with sour cream and honey or jam, though a savory version with herbs is also common.

faqs.q: Can I bake instead of fry these?
faqs.a: Yes — bake at 375°F on a parchment-lined sheet, flipping once, for a lighter version, though you'll lose some of the pan-fried crispness.
